Verification: content-checked (Complete main statement, date/byline, training/retrieval distinction, licence and sustainable-access positions inspected. Original proposed filing separately checked; no assertion of court acceptance or endorsement.). Limitations: Interested institutional position, not a court decision or empirical estimate of traffic, volunteer or publishing effects. A proposed legal distinction does not establish a universal rule for every training or retrieval system. Case- and jurisdiction-specific, not legal advice. Date basis: Publisher corporate byline and announcement date; distinct from 29 October court filing.

title: Motion for leave to file and proposed amicus curiae brief of Wikimedia Foundation in support of neither party
abstract: Requests separate use-specific fair-use analyses and contrasts model pre-training with substitutive retrieval. Footnote 24 expressly recognizes that licensed retrieval and other factual circumstances can change the analysis.
note: Method: proposed-amicus-legal-argument. Status: court-filing-not-a-ruling. Verification: content-checked (Commons version, 30-page file identity, original PDF filing stamps/cover, summary, conclusion and footnote 24 inspected. Uploader is not substituted for institutional author. Publication, filing and upload dates distinguished; no docket-status conclusion inferred.). Limitations: Advocacy attached to a motion seeking leave, not evidence that leave was granted or arguments adopted. Selected sections inspected, not a comprehensive legal audit. Benefits and ecosystem harms remain attributed; underlying studies and authorities were not all checked. Date basis: Court document filing stamps and motion date, not Commons upload or press statement on 30 October.
container-title: US District Court, Southern District of New York (copy hosted by Wikimedia Commons)

title: The 95% AI failure stat, one year later: junk number, real problem
abstract: Criticizes the widely repeated AI-pilot failure statistic and distinguishes adoption from financial impact. Combines a reported denominator critique with later surveys and argues for workflow redesign and explicit success criteria.
note: Method: commercial-practitioner-evidence-commentary. Status: blog-post. Verification: content-checked (Local Chrome main text, charts, captions, date/byline and source links inspected. Selected financial-impact and methods statements crosschecked against McKinsey's original survey; other survey series not comprehensively audited.). Limitations: Consulting interest and heterogeneous survey denominators. Correlations do not prove that workflow is the sole bottleneck; limited AI use does not itself establish unauthorized use. Underlying NANDA PDF and Wiblin critique were access-blocked and not independently read. No reconstructed failure rate adopted. Date basis: Visible corporate byline and date in local Chrome; no personal authorship inferred from contact links.

title: OpenAI just scooped mathematicians' work on another million-dollar problem
abstract: Reports competing AI-assisted work on Yang-Mills existence and a dispute about priority, private verification and release practices. The reported claim is narrower than the complete existence-and-mass-gap Millennium problem.
note: Method: science-reporting-with-researcher-interviews. Status: journalism. Verification: content-checked (Publisher main text through its breaking-news note, author/editor/date and current heading inspected in Chrome; some accessibility paragraph strings were clipped, so exhaustive full-text reading is not asserted. Claim scope checked against OpenAI's existing announcement and Clay's official formulation. No proof artifact executed or independently validated.). Limitations: Breaking-news reporting, not proof verification. Interviewees have differing institutional interests. Reported internal dates, formalization times and priority claims were not independently audited. Formal checking cannot be assumed to cover the intended physical statement; no inference of misconduct or prize eligibility is made. Date basis: Publisher date and personal byline inspected in Chrome; visible heading differs from URL/browser title.

title: The age of AI is forcing humanity to rethink what it means to be creative
abstract: Explains Zoran's distinction between creative artifacts and human development, including possible benefits for recipients. Explicitly identifies the underlying work as a philosophical framework rather than an experiment measuring transformation.
note: Method: research-explainer. Status: journalism. Verification: content-checked (Complete explainer, writer/editor/date, source link and explicit no-measurement qualification read. Primary paper identified and separately appraised; sidebar stories not admitted as evidence.). Limitations: Secondary explanation of one paper, not independent evidence of creativity gains or losses. Institutional writer credit and editorial role are distinct. Examples do not demonstrate psychological change or a universal history of creativity. Date basis: Publisher identifies HUJI Writer Yarden Mills separately from editor Shy Cohen; visible publication date.

title: Dutch Government Plans to Cut 25,000 Jobs in AI-Led Overhaul
abstract: Reports proposed civil-service reductions associated with AI and efficiency plans.
note: Method: policy-announcement-reporting. Status: journalism. Verification: content-checked (Local Chrome title, byline, dated public opening and government link inspected. Subscriber offer limited further reading; primary government statement checked separately.). Limitations: Public opening only; full subscriber text not read. Not an observed causal employment result. Use the separate government record for policy detail; no access restriction bypassed. Date basis: Local Chrome publisher byline and publication/update dates; tracking parameters removed.

title: More than we can make: generative AI, artistic forms, and artistic becoming
abstract: Argues that generative production can separate sophisticated artifacts from traditional apprenticeship. Distinguishes maker, recipient and cultural development, and proposes directing generative capability toward meaningful engagement rather than output abundance alone.
note: Method: philosophical-and-practice-based-normative-argument. Status: journal-article. Verification: content-checked (Journal author/date/DOI, abstract, decoupling clarifications, cultural limitation, proposed evaluation conditions and explicit no-measurement statement inspected. No empirical effects inferred from illustrative artworks.). Limitations: Conceptual and normative, not a controlled creativity or learning study. Interventions were not evaluated for transformation. Mainly Western historical framing is acknowledged. Suggested process proxies do not certify experience; a changed learning pathway is not necessarily no learning. Date basis: Journal's Published date, not the later press explainer.

title: Cabinet works towards an effective government: simpler, smarter and smaller
abstract: Sets multi-year savings targets corresponding to an estimated 25,000 FTE reduction. AI savings plans are due in the first quarter of 2027. The package also includes fewer rules, task choices, standardized ICT and property/office measures.
note: Method: official-government-policy-announcement. Status: policy-announcement. Verification: content-checked (Complete Dutch announcement read, including FTE units, multi-year timing, AI-planning paragraph, non-AI measures and exclusions. English summary is a translation, not an official English version; linked parliamentary letter not appraised.). Limitations: Government intentions and estimates, not realized savings or observed AI substitution. FTE is not a count of dismissed people. The package is multi-causal; announced future AI targets cannot establish that AI enables the whole reduction. Parliamentary letter not fully inspected. Date basis: Official dated government announcement.

title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
abstract: Survey of 1,719 participants in 97 nations contrasts widely reported individual productivity gains with 37% reporting enterprise EBIT contribution. Describes workflow-redesign associations, operating-cost constraints and differences between expected and retrospectively reported headcount reductions.
note: Method: international-online-business-survey. Status: industry-survey-report. Verification: content-checked (Publisher date/authors, report text, financial-impact distinctions, workforce comparison and About the research inspected. No underlying microdata audited; linked 31-page control returned the same article rather than a stable archived PDF.). Limitations: Self-reported attribution, not audited profit or causal ROI; consulting interest. GDP weighting does not make respondents representative of all firms. Cross-year comparisons are not all a fixed panel, although a 552-person repeat subgroup is reported. Absent EBIT attribution is not equivalent to project failure. Date basis: Current publisher article date; fieldwork May 4 to June 8, 2026. Rolling URL requires version checks.

title: Mathematics has changed. Let's act like it
abstract: Argues that AI expands feasible mathematical exploration and that institutions should reward understanding, worthwhile questions and exposition rather than paper counts alone. Proposes changes to evaluation, hiring, journals and training while retaining technical skills and criticizing poor attribution and unreliable output.
keyword: mathematics; science; learning; judgment; governance; work
note: Method: expert-normative-commentary. Status: guest-blog-post. Verification: content-checked (Full main post and notes read; date, guest authorship and distinction from the host's platform byline checked. Comments and linked proof claims not independently validated. Initial direct retrieval failed; opening the indexed canonical result returned the article.). Limitations: A normative expert position, not a causal study, disciplinary consensus or independent verification of OpenAI's mathematical claims. Proposed reforms have untested distributional effects; oral assessment can introduce bias. Collective credit does not settle specific attribution or access rights. Date basis: Visible publication date; guest-post introduction explicitly identifies Frank Calegari despite the platform's by Terence Tao label.

title: Metacognitive Scaffolds Create Productive Friction for AI-Assisted Knowledge Work
abstract: In a randomized study of 297 workers writing 594 essays, goal-setting and task-decomposition scaffolds improved writing despite lower perceived helpfulness and greater cognitive demand. The quality advantage persisted in a subsequent AI-assisted task without scaffolds.
note: Method: randomized-writing-experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv identity/version and HTML methods, task contrasts, judge validation, recall missingness and limitations inspected. Placeholder conference/DOI fields excluded; arXiv-issued DOI was marked pending registration.). Limitations: Not a test of transfer without AI. Quality scoring relies substantially on an LLM judge with moderate human agreement. Three-day topic recall is a shallow learning measure with substantial attrition and wide intervals; it does not establish durable expertise. Microsoft Research authors and short experimental tasks limit generalization. Date basis: arXiv v1 submission date, not the unfilled conference template's 2018 date. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2610.30945v1

title: The Effects of Generative AI on Collaboration and Social Networks Among Knowledge Workers
abstract: Digital collaboration records for 12,040 employees over 13 months associate a staged Copilot rollout with more collaboration, wider networks and greater reliance on historically strong ties. Difference-in-differences and fixed-effects instrumental-variable analyses address selection.
note: Method: organizational-rollout-quasi-experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv date/authors and HTML abstract, organization, period, Viva Insights measures and identification description inspected; no independent statistical reproduction. Pending DOI not treated as resolved.). Limitations: One focal unit of a consumer-products multinational. Identification depends on rollout and instrument assumptions. Calls, email and meeting measures do not directly establish useful collaboration, productivity or welfare; more communication may help or impose costs. Date basis: arXiv v1 submission date; observation period is September 2024 to September 2025. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2610.32461v1

title: Developer Task Delegation to LLMs and the Trust Factor: A Mixed Methods Study
abstract: Twenty-two interviews and 160 survey responses distinguish full and partial delegation, doing work oneself, and avoiding tasks. Trust is associated with delegation choices, illustrating why access is not equivalent to actual task use.
note: Method: interviews-and-practitioner-survey. Status: preprint-author-reports-icse-2027-acceptance. Verification: content-checked (arXiv author/version/acceptance statement and HTML recruitment, collection dates, delegation definitions and scale reliability inspected. No proceedings DOI inferred from the acceptance comment.). Limitations: Self-reported choices, not measured correctness or a causal effect of trust. Most survey respondents came from Prolific; interview and survey collection spans 2024 to May 2026 rather than exclusively the latest agent workflows. Within-person trust measurement reliability is modest. Date basis: arXiv v1 submission date; reported ICSE 2027 acceptance is not a 2026 proceedings publication. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2610.34317v1

title: Developers as Managers of AI Agents: A Workplace Shadowing Study
abstract: Eleven developers were observed for approximately 15 hours, with 255 prompts and follow-up interviews. Prompt formulation and response checking occupied 33.4% of observed time. Supervisor, delegator and learner patterns show redistribution of work rather than disappearance of human control.
note: Method: workplace-shadowing-and-follow-up-interviews. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (Versioned HTML author/date, abstract, observed-time denominator, interview component and study-design structure inspected. No causal productivity estimate extracted.). Limitations: Small descriptive sample and short observation window, without a no-AI comparison. Management time is not automatically waste or evidence of a net slowdown. Colleagues remain sources of organizational authority and alignment, not merely technical information. Date basis: arXiv v1 date; unfilled proceedings template fields not used. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2610.33588v1

title: "To Boldly Go Where No One Has Gone Before" What Has AI Let Developers Unlock?
abstract: A survey of 331 Microsoft developers distinguishes faster familiar work, work previously out of reach and new agent-oriented work. It proposes evaluating expanded possibilities as well as speed, while preserving developers' ability to judge delegated output.
note: Method: developer-survey-and-reflexive-thematic-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (Official Microsoft Research summary and canonical arXiv author list, v1 date and abstract inspected; HTML contents checked. Detailed coding and appendix not independently audited.). Limitations: Single-employer self-reports and AI-assisted thematic analysis, not randomized output measurement. Themes and a proposed playbook do not establish durable learning, realized business value or longitudinal deskilling. Authors' organizational relationship to AI tooling matters. Date basis: arXiv v1 submission; Microsoft Research landing page independently identifies October 2026. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2610.23708v1

title: A Preliminary Analysis of the Impact of AI Assisted/Generated Code on Quality, Centrality and Review Time at Scale
abstract: Meta code-provenance analysis links landed AI completions with review and production incidents. AI-assisted changes differ systematically in language, size, authorship and code context. Faster reviews and lower incident associations cannot be read as unconfounded causal gains.
note: Method: code-provenance-and-context-adjusted-observational-analysis. Status: conference-paper. Verification: content-checked (Publisher authors/date/DOI and 23-page PDF inspected selectively: abstract, review/SEV results, validity and discussion/conclusion. Completion-era scope and centrality qualifications retained; no independent data reproduction.). Limitations: Pre-agentic completion tools, one firm's repository and internal infrastructure; observational adjustment cannot eliminate selection. The centrality association is small and measure-sensitive. Does not invalidate other organizations' adverse findings or establish current agentic code safety. Authors have Meta affiliations. Date basis: Dagstuhl publication date.
container-title: 20th International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM 2026)

title: Faster, Higher, Stronger? The Impact of GenAI on Knowledge Work Productivity - Evidence from the Field
abstract: Among 128 knowledge workers in an industrial organization, AI improved efficiency across acquisition, packaging and creation tasks, but quality improved only for packaging and creation and declined for acquisition. Speed and quality therefore require separate reporting.
note: Method: randomized-lab-in-the-field-experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv metadata and public PDF checked for randomization/task comparison, underlying model, fieldwork period, fixed order and limitations. No pooled effect size inferred.). Limitations: Standardized tasks within one organization, fixed task order and an early-2025 GPT-4o mini/RAG implementation. Neither a universal capability boundary nor an evaluation of October 2026 frontier models. Long-term outcomes and naturalistic use remain unmeasured. Date basis: arXiv v1 date; experiment conducted in early 2025. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2607.25922v1

title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
abstract: A 200-participant writing experiment varies AI availability and reward structure. Originality incentives increase collective diversity relative to quality-only incentives, with more selective adoption of generated text. Human incentives can modify homogenization rather than merely accept it.
note: Method: preregistered-factorial-creative-writing-experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (Versioned HTML authors/date, preregistration distinction, 2x2 design, recruitment, sample and task duration inspected. No claim that every reported analysis was preregistered.). Limitations: Brief Prolific stories are not scientific discoveries or a long-run creative ecosystem. Diversity metrics, quality and originality are different outcomes. Some analyses are exploratory despite preregistration; mechanism interpretation is not itself a separately randomized intervention. Date basis: arXiv v1 submission date. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2604.03529v1

title: Firm Data on AI
abstract: The October revision covers nearly 9,000 executives in seven countries, with 78% reporting firm AI use. It reports modest retrospective productivity effects and little aggregate net employment effect, alongside expected gains and offsetting firm-level employment changes.
note: Method: multi-country-executive-survey. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (Local Chrome title, issue/revision months, DOI and revised abstract opening checked against the complete current publisher-indexed abstract and author list. Revision mismatch caught and corrected before admission; no full-paper appraisal asserted.). Limitations: Executive reports and forecasts, not audited causal effects or proof of no job displacement. Earlier roughly 6,000-executive/four-country findings are superseded for this intake. Full revised paper not read: ordinary web retrieval was blocked and Chrome exposed only a truncated abstract; the complete publisher-indexed abstract supplied the remaining claims and author list. Date basis: NBER issue and revision months; no exact day invented.

title: What Work Does Generative AI Do?
abstract: Nationally representative survey evidence links actual reported AI use to tasks and occupations. Adoption is broad but shallow and heterogeneous among similar workers. Occupational exposure scores and provider chat logs are not interchangeable with task-level adoption measures.
note: Method: representative-worker-task-adoption-survey. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (NBER local Chrome title, authors, DOI, issue month and abstract opening; SSRN public full abstract and dates; earlier Fed summary inspected. No full paper downloaded or subscription bypassed.). Limitations: Self-reported adoption, not a causal productivity or employment estimate. Public abstracts and metadata read, not the full paper; earlier Fed dissemination and later NBER/SSRN versions must not be counted as independent evidence or assumed textually identical. Date basis: NBER issue month and SSRN Date Written; earlier Fed dissemination is separately dated July 2026.

title: Does AI Actually Free up Workers' Time?
abstract: Interview with researcher Aruna Ranganathan describes work expansion, blurred boundaries and multitasking in an eight-month study with Xingqi Maggie Ye. More than 40 interviews at a 200-person company suggest that enabling more work need not free workers' time.
note: Method: institutional-researcher-interview-about-ethnography. Status: research-interview. Verification: content-checked (Complete short institutional Q&A, named researchers, byline/date, interview count, fieldwork duration and distinction between expanded capability and reduced workload inspected. Linked HBR article not treated as separately read full text.). Limitations: Public researcher interview, not a peer-reviewed causal estimate. Company size is not interview sample size. One setting and qualitative observations cannot establish population burnout prevalence or imply that all expanded work is unwanted. Proposed interventions remain untested here. Date basis: Berkeley byline and publication date.

title: The shift toward open and reproducible AI research
abstract: Analysis of 56,800 papers from five AI conferences, 2014-2024, finds improving artifact-sharing and documentation. An LLM-based classification pipeline makes large-scale meta-research possible; a manually labelled 160-paper sample checks its performance.
note: Method: llm-assisted-longitudinal-documentation-analysis. Status: journal-article. Verification: content-checked (Publisher authors/date/DOI, corpus window, documentation-analysis method, manual validation and distinction between artifact sharing and estimated reproducibility inspected. No independent replication of classification.). Limitations: Estimated reproducibility is a documentation-based proxy calibrated from earlier work, not actual rerunning of 56,800 studies. Trends and checklist associations do not establish policy causality. Published in 2026 but data end in 2024; classifier errors and changing conference composition matter. Date basis: Publisher publication date.

title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
abstract: Paper2Agent turns paper-associated resources into callable tools. Seventy-four of 100 computational-biology papers were agentified; a tutorial-derived benchmark favored the structured approach over direct repository access. Missing artifacts and environment failures limited coverage.
note: Method: research-tool-development-and-comparative-benchmark. Status: journal-article. Verification: content-checked (Journal identity, author/date/DOI, corpus sizes, successful-agentification definition, tutorial-derived ground truth and direct-repository baseline inspected. Supplements, underlying code and scientific claims not independently reproduced.). Limitations: Developer-run benchmark, not an independent researcher productivity trial. Tutorial execution fidelity does not validate original science or demonstrate novel discovery. Success on the agentified subset must not hide unsuccessful papers; automated tool checks are narrower than scientific correctness. Date basis: Publisher version-of-record date, not acceptance or submission.

title: Energy use of AI inference, efficiency pathways, and test-time scaling
abstract: Models optimized production-scale inference and efficiency pathways. Short-query energy can be substantially lower than poorly matched estimates, while long reasoning and agentic workloads increase demand. Per-query efficiency does not determine aggregate resource use.
note: Method: assumption-dependent-inference-energy-model. Status: journal-article. Verification: content-checked (Official Microsoft Research title, eight authors and journal/DOI link crosschecked with Crossref metadata; public abstract and authors' Zenodo scope caveats read. Publisher full text returned 403; June repository version not presumed identical to the journal article.). Limitations: Microsoft-affiliated authors. Read public institutional abstract and related author repository description, not full journal text. Assumption-dependent modeled inference, not universal metering, marginal carbon or a full lifecycle assessment. Efficiency opportunities are not guaranteed reductions in total demand. Date basis: Microsoft Research identifies Joule April 2026; Crossref issue date is August 2026. Distinct online/issue timing retained without inventing an exact day.

title: Disruption without dividend? - How the digital divide and task differences split GenAI's global impact
abstract: Across 135 countries, task composition and internet access qualify occupational exposure estimates. Connectivity gaps may block augmentation benefits while connected workers remain exposed to automation. Identical occupation labels do not imply identical tasks across economies.
note: Method: cross-country-exposure-and-digital-access-analysis. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (ILO author/date/DOI and detailed findings inspected; World Bank reproducibility catalog identity checked. Publication, news and package dates distinguished; underlying exposure calculations not rerun.). Limitations: Potential exposure and infrastructure constraints, not observed job displacement, adoption or realized productivity. Read the institutional abstract and detailed findings, not the complete paper or reproducibility package. ILO and World Bank versions describe one study family, not independent replications. Date basis: ILO publication page, not the 27 March news announcement or January reproducibility-package production date.

title: Energy use of AI inference - estimates and efficiency opportunities
abstract: Explains why energy disclosures with different workload and accounting boundaries cannot be compared directly. Agent workflows may turn one user request into many inference, retrieval and verification steps, undermining simplistic per-query comparisons.
note: Method: expert-methodological-commentary. Status: blog-post. Verification: content-checked (Byline/date and public sections on comparison boundaries, output lengths and hidden agent calls inspected; primary study separately identified. No independent energy measurements performed.). Limitations: Selected public explanatory sections read, not an independent experiment or a complete audit of every cited energy estimate. Discussion substantially concerns Oviedo and colleagues' paper and must not be counted as a second empirical result. Date basis: Publisher date and named byline.

title: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell. Brotli flaw (CVE-2026-111497) blast radius affects many libraries & apps using HTTP.
abstract: Explains Python and other downstream paths to the shared Brotli decoder, including optional dependencies and HTTP response decoding. Connects package updates with rebuilds and verification of running workloads.
note: Method: vendor-technical-synthesis. Status: security-analysis. Verification: content-checked (Publication/update dates, corporate byline, Python sections and mitigation caveats inspected. Selected package versions checked against GitHub's reviewed advisory and API; both PyPA/OSV records inspected for aliases and range differences. No packages installed, payloads executed or vendor images adopted.). Limitations: Commercial vendor promoting its own scanner and images. Installation is not sufficient evidence of reachable attacker-controlled decoding. Download counts are not exposed installations. Python decoder tests are not a complete RCE demonstration; dated no-exploitation remarks must not override current KEV status. Not every product or patch-table entry independently checked. Date basis: Publisher explicitly distinguishes publication on 23 October from last update on 27 October.

title: Brotli: Out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder ("Node2Shell") also affects the PyPI Brotli package
abstract: Reviewed advisory maps affected PyPI brotli and brotlicffi packages to fixed versions 1.2.1 and 1.2.1.0. Supplies machine-readable package identity for dependency scanning.
note: Method: reviewed-package-advisory. Status: security-advisory. Verification: content-checked (Reviewed GitHub page and structured API checked for package names, ranges, fixes, timestamps and null CVE field. Both linked OSV records checked for CVE/GHSA aliases and package-specific fixes; database claims not independently reproduced.). Limitations: Not independent discovery or proof of exposure in every installed environment. GitHub's API cve_id is null despite the description and OSV mapping identifying the shared CVE. GitHub and PyPA/OSV differ on lower affected bounds; no silent reconciliation. Database presence does not guarantee a particular scanner has updated or checked all running copies. Date basis: Advisory API published_at and updated_at, distinguished from package release or discovery dates.

title: Brotli2Shell: Frequently asked questions for Google Brotli decoder vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497)
abstract: Maps Brotli2Shell, Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell to one CVE and surveys downstream exposure and release paths.
note: Method: expert-advisory-synthesis. Status: security-analysis. Verification: content-checked (Publisher date, byline, alias mapping, dependency distinctions and dated exploitation/KEV qualifications inspected; current catalog status checked separately against official JSON.). Limitations: Cross-product synthesis, not independent discovery or reproduction of every affected product. Its 26 October statement that the CVE was not in KEV is superseded by CISA's 27 October addition. Linked third-party exploitation claims retain their original uncertainty. Date basis: Publisher date and named author.

title: RCE via OOM corruption
abstract: Maintainer-confirmed PHP memory-corruption issue associated with out-of-memory handling and unauthenticated remote code execution under affected conditions.
note: Method: maintainer-security-advisory. Status: security-advisory. Verification: content-checked (Maintainer description, version ranges, credits and stable identifiers inspected; publication metadata crosschecked through GitHub API.). Limitations: Affected versions and demonstrated paths do not count vulnerable websites or successful compromises. Advisory inspected, exploit not reproduced. Date basis: Maintainer advisory published_at verified through GitHub API.

title: RCE via stale global state
abstract: Documents stale request-owned state surviving fatal-error cleanup and subsequent unsafe reuse, with configuration-dependent memory disclosure, corruption or code execution.
note: Method: maintainer-security-advisory. Status: security-advisory. Verification: content-checked (Maintainer advisory identity, description and affected/fixed branches inspected; CVE and published_at verified through GitHub API.). Limitations: Not a universal exploitability claim. Separate variants and configuration requirements matter; later PHP notices must also be consulted. Exploit not reproduced. Date basis: Maintainer advisory published_at verified through GitHub API.

title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
abstract: Traces signs of the OOM issue to 2024, subsequent AI-assisted exploit demonstrations, resource and decision bottlenecks, fixes and disrupted disclosure.
note: Method: maintainer-incident-retrospective. Status: maintainer-report. Verification: content-checked (Dated maintainer account, historical discovery, reporting timeline, staffing and disclosure sections inspected. Embedded social-media responses are not adopted as evidence.). Limitations: Participant account, not an independent incident investigation. Claims about other parties' disclosure conduct remain attributed; no causal attribution of attacks to a particular leak is established. Date basis: Publisher date and corporate byline.

title: How the PHP Security Team Handles Your Reports
abstract: Describes human reproduction and classification of security reports, welcoming validated AI-assisted submissions while reporting 15 published CVEs and 106 closed non-vulnerability, duplicate or non-reproducing reports since July.
note: Method: maintainer-workflow-report. Status: maintainer-report. Verification: content-checked (Byline, date, report counts, classification discussion and AI-report guidance inspected; no access to the private submission queue.). Limitations: The 106 are not an AI false-positive count or rate: submissions have mixed origins and outcomes. Not a measured workload comparison with a no-AI counterfactual. Date basis: Publisher date and named byline.

title: PHP2Shell: A tale of two PHP remote vulnerabilities
abstract: Describes human-directed AI-assisted variant analysis informed by PHP vulnerability history, leading to reproducible exploit paths and coordinated reporting.
note: Method: discoverer-technical-case-study. Status: technical-blog. Verification: content-checked (Research index date, explicit writing credit, discovery history, method and application/SAPI distinctions inspected. No exploit code executed or downloaded.). Limitations: Researcher account without a controlled human-only comparison. Initial discovery used generally available models; human expertise and target selection remain material. Technical claims not independently reproduced here. Date basis: Dated entry in Calif's research index; write-up credits Ryan Austin. August discovery dates are not publication dates.

title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
abstract: Reports AI-assisted discovery, adaptation and lab demonstrations of PHP exploit chains across representative applications, with a responsible-disclosure timeline.
note: Method: discoverer-technical-case-study. Status: technical-blog. Verification: content-checked (Author/date, impact table, AI-method discussion, disclosed model involvement and timeline inspected. Marketing sections and uninspected demonstrations not treated as independently verified outcomes.). Limitations: Title overgeneralizes prevalence as affected share. Selected demonstrations are not an internet-wide compromise census. Research-effort comparisons are retrospective estimates, not randomized evidence; commercial and model-provider interests apply. Date basis: Publisher author list and date.

title: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
abstract: Reports a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry on 17 October, before public disclosure, while leaving real-world success and the actor's information source unresolved.
note: Method: first-party-threat-telemetry. Status: security-research-blog. Verification: content-checked (Dated threat-intelligence report, attempt timestamps and explicit uncertainty about successful exploitation inspected; raw sensor data not audited.). Limitations: Attempt is not confirmed compromise. Anonymized infrastructure does not establish attribution, a leak source or AI use by an attacker. No representative attack-success denominator. Date basis: Publisher date and CJ Moses byline.

title: Obstacles to Weaponizing PHP2Shell Likely Constrain Immediate Widespread Exploitation
abstract: Separates crash demonstrations, laboratory RCE and reliable exploitation across deployments; reports no successful wild exploitation observed in its scope as of 23 October.
note: Method: first-party-exploitability-assessment. Status: security-research-blog. Verification: content-checked (Date, authors, laboratory-versus-wild distinction, configuration barriers and assessment inspected. Technical reproductions not repeated.). Limitations: Dated sensor-limited negative observation, not proof of no exploitation globally. Later KEV entries supersede a present-tense no-exploitation claim, without invalidating the earlier observation. Date basis: Publisher date and author block.

title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
abstract: Reports unsuccessful chains in its own telemetry, acknowledges stronger public honeypot RCE evidence elsewhere, and describes declining observed exposure without attributing the decline solely to patches.
note: Method: first-party-threat-and-exposure-telemetry. Status: security-research-blog. Verification: content-checked (Full article, authors, date, exposure definitions, unsuccessful-attempt analysis and acknowledgement of external RCE evidence read in Chrome. No exploit kit executed.). Limitations: Own telemetry is not global absence. Changing coverage, network restriction and retirement affect exposure trends. Public honeypot success under favorable conditions does not establish universal reliability. Date basis: Publisher time element and bylines inspected in Chrome.

title: Censys PHP2Shell Exposure Tracker
abstract: Provides version-inferred service exposure and observed transitions to fixed versions, with explicit qualifications about hidden versions, backports, scan lag and counting units.
note: Method: internet-scan-exposure-dashboard. Status: live-dashboard. Verification: content-checked (Loaded dashboard timestamp, service counts and complete notes/limitations inspected in Chrome; stale search-index counts not used as current data.). Limitations: Services are not unique websites, machines or organizations. Reported versions are not exploitability tests. Detection changes and hidden versions limit inference; observed upgrades lag actual deployment. Date basis: Dated observation of evolving dashboard, not a claimed first-publication date.

title: Usage statistics of PHP for websites
